headline: Red Flag Warning Issued for Los Angeles and Ventura Counties as Santa Ana Winds and Heat Wave Raise Extreme Fire Risk Through Saturday
overview: A dangerous combination of strengthening Santa Ana winds, low humidity, and unseasonable warmth is driving extreme fire weather conditions across Southern California through the weekend, while a M6.1 earthquake struck off Japan's Pacific coast today and a rare wildfire spread to nearly 1,000 acres in New Hampshire's White Mountains. Flooding emergencies continue across multiple US states from Florida to New Jersey, and ongoing volcanic activity at Kīlauea and Mayon keeps alert levels elevated in Hawaii and the Philippines.

events.title: Red Flag Warning — Santa Ana Winds and Extreme Fire Risk
events.location: Los Angeles and Ventura Counties, Southern California, USA
events.summary: The National Weather Service issued a Red Flag Warning for the Santa Clarita Valley, Santa Monica Mountains, Santa Susana Mountains, and western San Gabriel Mountains through Saturday evening, November 7, as Santa Ana winds are forecast to peak with gusts of 30–45 mph, accompanied by very low relative humidity and warming temperatures. Conditions are expected to allow rapid fire growth and extreme fire behavior with any new ignition, particularly late Friday night through Saturday. The event coincides with a broader heat wave arriving in Southern California and elevated wildfire risk across the urban-wildland interface of one of the most densely populated regions in the US.

events.title: M 6.1 Earthquake — Off Japan's Pacific Coast Near Hasaki
events.summary: A magnitude 6.1 earthquake struck 144 km southeast of Hasaki, Japan at 10:39 UTC on November 6, at a depth of 29 km, generating shaking reported across multiple prefectures along Japan's Pacific coast. USGS assigned a green alert level and no tsunami alert was issued, but 27 felt reports were logged, indicating the event was widely perceived. The quake occurred in a seismically active subduction zone offshore of Honshu, and no significant damage reports had emerged as of the time of this report.

events.title: Wild River Fire — Rare Wildfire Spreads to ~1,000 Acres in White Mountains
events.location: White Mountain National Forest, near Gorham, New Hampshire, USA
events.summary: A wildfire in the White Mountain National Forest near Gorham, New Hampshire grew to nearly 1,000 acres, an exceptionally rare event for a region where large wildfires are almost unheard of. Local fire officials described the blaze as unlike anything in recent memory for the area, noting that wildfires of this scale do not occur in the White Mountains under normal conditions. The cause and containment status are under active assessment by forest fire crews.

events.title: Kīlauea Episode 56 — Lava Fountaining Ends After ~6 Hours
events.summary: Episode 56 of Kīlauea's ongoing episodic eruption began at approximately 12:10 p.m. HST on November 5 and ended abruptly at 6:01 p.m. HST — lasting roughly six hours of lava fountaining at Halemaʻumaʻu Crater before ceasing. This marks a notable resolution from yesterday's elevated WATCH alert status issued by the Hawaiian Volcano Observatory, which had anticipated imminent fountaining. The eruption remains within the confines of Hawaiʻi Volcanoes National Park and poses no direct threat to populated areas; however, the ongoing episodic eruption cycle — now in its 56th episode since December 2024 — continues to be closely monitored.

events.title: Flash Flooding — New Jersey Coast and Northeast US
events.location: Monmouth and Ocean Counties, New Jersey, USA
events.summary: A Flash Flood Warning was issued this morning for Monmouth and Ocean Counties in New Jersey after more than 3 inches of rain fell in a short period, closing major roadways including NJ-35 in Belmar, NJ-71 in Manasquan, and ramps along I-195 in Wall Township. PSE&G reported over 15,600 customers without power across New Jersey, with additional outages logged by JCP&L. A broader Flood Watch was also active across southeastern Massachusetts and Rhode Island through Saturday morning, as a frontal system tracked up the Northeast coastline.

events.title: Mayon Volcano — Massive Ash Cloud, 13 Earthquakes, Sustained Displacement
events.summary: Mayon Volcano continues to escalate its eruptive activity, with fresh reports of a massive ash cloud ejected to significant altitude and 13 volcanic earthquakes recorded in the latest 24-hour monitoring window, adding to concerns about a more explosive phase. Thousands of evacuees remain displaced across Albay Province with humanitarian operations ongoing. Philippine authorities have maintained elevated alert levels, and ashfall continues to affect surrounding municipalities.

events.title: Pacific Northwest Storm Watch — 50-Knot Gusts and 26-Foot Seas Incoming
events.location: Washington and Oregon Coast (Cape Flattery to Cape Falcon), USA
events.summary: The National Weather Service has issued Storm Watches for Washington and Oregon coastal waters from Cape Flattery to Cape Falcon, with dangerous conditions expected to arrive Saturday, November 7 through Sunday, November 8. Forecast conditions include south winds of 30–40 knots with gusts to 50 knots and seas of 21–26 feet, posing a significant hazard to maritime operations and coastal communities. The system is associated with the active El Niño-enhanced atmospheric river pattern and follows a week of elevated storm activity along the Pacific Coast.
